a plan for the next year
senses.definition: How things really work somewhere new, who decides and what has already been tried.
senses.caution: It is fine in your first month but sounds like stalling later. Do not use it in an update where people are waiting for a decision or asking about results.
senses.example: Give me two weeks with the delivery leads to get the lay of the land before I propose any changes.

cues.text: You have joined a new organisation and want to describe the first month as working out who decides what before you propose anything.
Before a customer workshop you ask a colleague to brief you on the politics and the history you will be walking into.
You have moved to a new neighbourhood and spend a fortnight finding which shops, which routes and which neighbours matter.
A friend starting at a new school asks how long it takes before things stop feeling foreign.

distractors: The published organisation chart, showing who reports to whom.
A map of which systems talk to which, drawn before any change is made.
A list of every system a team owns, kept up to date for audit purposes.
A survey of what competitors are selling and at what price, refreshed every quarter.
The full list of everything a team has agreed to deliver this quarter, ranked in order.
